title: Goldman Sachs Sees U.S. Natural Gas Demand Surging on Data Center Boom | OilPrice.com

Data center proliferation will drive demand for natural gas in the United States over the next two years, Goldman Sachs has forecast, estimating that some 52 GW of new data center capacity could be added to the grid in 2028 alone.

“Year-to-date, data-center power capacity and demand have increased by nearly 30% in the US, contributing to more than one third of US total power demand growth,” the bank’s analysts wrote in a note this week, as cited by Reuters. “We expect growth acceleration in data centers to be driven not only by a higher volume of facilities, but by increasingly larger physical footprints and higher power density,” they said.

This will drive stronger growth in demand for electricity and, by extension, for natural gas, which has become the preferred method for data center operators to source reliable, baseload electricity since nuclear takes too long to build.

That data centers are massive energy demand sources is no news. Indeed, data centers are the primary reason for upbeat demand growth projections in the natural gas industry. U.S. gas-fired power generation capacity in development directly tied to data centers nearly doubled to 189 GW in the first half of the year, and chances are the momentum continued in the second half as well. Data center operators like natural gas. And natural gas producers like data centers.

No wonder, then, that U.S. natural gas production is on track to close a second consecutive year with record-high natural gas output as producers respond to demand signs both at home and overseas.

Soaring demand for powering data centers combined with rising liquefied natural gas exports amid expanding liquefaction capacity, as well as surging global demand for spot LNG cargoes in the absence of Qatar’s gas due to the Iran war, is pushing American natural gas production higher this year.
